narrative: Material PL1__M4174A5C shows smooth, high-volume daily demand averaging 26,786 units per working day with a CV of 0.356, indicating moderate but regular variability. A slight declining trend was detected over the observation period. Lead times are short (mean 2.36 days) and relatively stable (CV 0.480). The current SAP policy holds zero safety stock, leaving the material exposed to stockouts. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity capped at the storage capacity constraint provides the optimal balance of ordering and holding costs while achieving the 95% service level.
warnings: Declining demand trend detected — monitor for sustained reduction before next policy review.
EOQ (583,293) exceeded by storage capacity constraint — order quantity capped at 473,084 units.
6 demand outliers detected and winsorised at 1st/99th percentile.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and near-continuous (CV=0.356, 100% non-zero days) making the classical (r,Q) model with EOQ the analytically optimal choice. The normal approximation for safety stock is appropriate given the unimodal demand distribution and sufficient data volume (96 observations).
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity caps the unconstrained EOQ of 583,293 to 473,084 units. This increases ordering frequency from ~11.5 to ~14.2 orders/year, adding approximately $195 in annual ordering costs. Service level impact is negligible as safety stock is unaffected.
